en.title: Dexter's Dark Universe: Every Spinoff Explained Before Original Sin Arrives
en.summary: With the Dexter universe expanding, it's time to get your bearings. From the original serial killer's bloody trail to his shadowy past, we break down every chapter of the Dexter saga.
en.body:
The world of **Dexter** is expanding, and with **Dexter: Original Sin** on the horizon, it's the perfect time to revisit the blood-spattered timeline. Showtime may be gone, but the chilling legacy of Dexter Morgan lives on, primarily on Paramount+. Whether you're a seasoned viewer who remembers every kill or a curious newcomer drawn in by the latest prequel, understanding the order of events is crucial to appreciating the intricate, dark tapestry of this franchise.

## Navigating the Dexter Timeline
The original **Dexter** series, which ran for eight seasons from 2006 to 2013, introduced us to the Miami Metro homicide detective with a dark passenger. Michael C. Hall embodied the titular character, a forensic blood spatter analyst who moonlights as a vigilante serial killer, adhering to a strict code. The series, while lauded for its initial seasons, is infamous for its divisive ending. The narrative picked up again eight years later in **Dexter: New Blood** (2021), a miniseries set in upstate New York. Here, Dexter lived under an assumed identity until his past, and his son Harrison, came calling, leading to a new set of icy, suspenseful confrontations.

## The Genesis of the Dark Passenger
Now, **Dexter: Original Sin** promises to take us back to the very beginning. This upcoming prequel will explore Dexter's formative years as a young college student entering the Miami Metro homicide forensics department. We'll witness his early struggles with his homicidal urges and see him forge relationships with the familiar faces who will populate his original series. Christian Slater is set to play a younger Harry Morgan, guiding Dexter through his first kills and teaching him the foundational elements of the code. Molly Brown will portray a young Debra Morgan, and we'll also see younger iterations of characters like LaGuerta, Batista, and Masuka. Michael C. Hall's iconic inner narration is confirmed to return, providing that essential, chilling perspective.

This prequel isn't just a look back; it functions as an extended flashback, bridging the gap between the events of **Dexter: New Blood** and the original series' timeline. The casting for **Dexter: Original Sin** has been met with excitement, hinting at a faithful yet fresh exploration of the character's origins. The intricate connections between these series are what make the **Dexter** universe so compelling for its dedicated fanbase, offering layers of narrative depth for both long-time followers and new viewers.

## What's Next
While **Dexter: Original Sin** is set to premiere in 2025, details regarding its exact release date and specific streaming platform beyond its initial network are still emerging. Fans eagerly await more information as the franchise continues to expand its dark, compelling narrative.

content_raw: Dexter: Resurrection is coming back this month, but what does that mean!? Which Dexter is THIS Dexter? Wait, HOW many Dexter s are there? Well, buckle up, friends, because I’m going to take you through the different spinoffs. The original series aired on Showtime, which no longer exists. Where can you watch them now? They live on Paramount+. I present them to you here, in chronological order. 1. Dexter This is the original one, the OG Dexter. Four perfect seasons followed by one dicey-but-okay season followed by a genuinely terrible season followed by a pretty good season followed by a genuinely demented ending. That’s eight seasons, and that’s Dexter . Number of seasons: 8 Years: 2006-2013 Setting: Miami, FL Who plays Dexter?: Michael C. Hall   2. Dexter: New Blood Picking up EIGHT years after the series finale, Dexter: New Blood is about how Dexter has been living under an assumed name in a basically-Canadian backwater of upstate New York when his teenaged son (remember little Harrison from the original series?) suspects that he might not actually be dead and comes to look for him. Lots of ice-cold suspense in this one. Number of seasons: 1 Years: 2021 Setting: Upstate New York Who plays Dexter?: Michael C. Hall   3. Dexter: Original Sin Dexter: Original Sin is a throwback! It’s an origin story, about collegiate Dexter getting his first job at the Miami homicide forensics department, and making friends with/getting to know all the folks he’ll come to work with in the regular series, which takes place years later. Although the series is technically a prequel, it functions as an extended flashback sequence between the events of Dexter: New Blood , and Dexter: Resurrection. The casting in this thing is incredible … characters genuinely look like younger versions of the characters we know from the series (especially James Martinez’s Angel Batista… wow, he gets David Zayas’s voice down perfectly). But despite the marvels of its aesthetic continuity, a lot of the show’s narrative is a bit revisionist, changing details we remember from (or literally saw in flashbacks in) the original series. I also don’t love the central mystery, but hey, what can you do? Number of seasons: 1 Years: 2024-2025 Setting: Miami, Fl Who plays Dexter?: Patrick Gibson and Michael C. Hall   4. Dexter: Resurrection Ah, and now were come to the current beast! Dexter: Resurrection comes after the brouhaha of New Blood (and after the extended flashback frame of Dexter: Original Sin ), bringing our antihero to New York City, where he must stop a serial killer who seems to have a connection to a whole bunch of serial killers. Oh, and work out things with his son. That’s all I’ll say. Number of seasons: 2 Years: 2025-current Setting: New York City Who plays Dexter?: Michael C. Hall
